title: Edge Observability Aggregator for Dedicated & Private: checkpointed, replayable, tenant-scoped dedupe and low-latency fanout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an edge-side observability aggregator that runs in per-customer perimeter (VPC/on-prem) to provide deterministic deduplication, lightweight checkpointing for replay, tenant-scoped retention control, and low-latency fanout to Redwood ingest endpoints. This reduces duplicate traces/logs coming from instrumented services (esp. on noisy private networks), enables safe offline replay for debugging/regression detection, and gives platform teams a controllable ingest burst buffer without violating tenant isolation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Aggregator deployed as an optional standalone binary/sidecar with a minimal config for Dedicated and Private installs. 2) Checkpoint files encrypted at rest and exportable for secure replay. 3) End-to-end test shows at least 60% reduction in duplicate spans for a noisy synthetic workload. 4) Replay mode can rehydrate checkpoints and push to a chosen runtime-1.20-compatible ingest endpoint with configurable rate limit. 5) Per-tenant retention/forwarding policies are enforceable and audited in console logs.
design_decisions:
- Chosen proto envelope (compact protobuf) for wire format to support schema evolution and small memory footprint.
- Local dedupe uses a time-windowed LRU bloom + lightweight sequence watermark; avoids global coordination to preserve private deployment isolation.
- Checkpointing is incremental, encrypted with KMS/HSM-backed keys when available; fallback to file-wrapped AES-GCM with per-tenant key material.
- Fanout to Redwood uses gRPC with per-tenant mTLS and optional mutual-auth rotation; fall back to HTTPS if firewall rules prevent gRPC.
- No persistent cross-tenant indexing; metadata shards are tenant-scoped to meet compliance needs.
- Replay respects original timing by supporting 'speedup' parameter and a safe-rate cap to avoid overwhelming upstream in bursty replays.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Local dedupe may under-deduplicate if clock drift is extreme; mitigation: include span origin fingerprint and monotonic counters where available.
- Checkpoint files increase disk usage; we add a configurable eviction policy and compact-on-dump to minimize storage.
- Replay could expose PII if redaction rules mismatch; we require pluggable scrubber extensions and a pre-replay dry-run verification step.
- Adds operational surface area for Dedicated customers; doc+runbooks required for support teams.
implementation_notes:
- New aggregator written in Rust for low memory overhead and deterministic shutdown behavior.
- Library used: tonic for gRPC, prost for protobuf, rust-crypto for AES-GCM.
- CLI supports modes: collect (edge runtime), checkpoint, replay, inspect.
- Integrates with existing perimeter-forwarder mTLS cert rotation and private KMS plugin.
- Metrics exported via Prometheus endpoint: aggregator_dedupe_rate, aggregator_checkpoint_size_bytes, aggregator_replay_ops_total, aggregator_backpressure_seconds.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for dedupe primitives and checkpoint encryption.
2) Integration test harness simulating multi-service duplicate span bursts (k6-based workload).
3) E2E staging deploy to a Dedicated customer cluster with synthetic noise to validate dedupe % and replay correctness.
4) Chaos test: restart aggregator during checkpointing to validate atomicity and resume.
5) Security audit for checkpoint encryption and scrubber rules.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal dogfood in Redwood-managed Dedicated region (2 clusters) behind a feature flag.
Phase 2: early access for 2 enterprise customers with signed MSA and dedicated onboarding.
Phase 3: general availability in runtime-1.20 with opt-in toggle in Console.
Rollback: disable feature flag and allow automatic fallback to perimeter-forwarder; provide a migration tool to export/import checkpointed state.
